title: Appeal of RE Charles Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC reversed Korean Capital Presbytery’s and its Special Judicial Commission’s actions adjudicating Kim guilty and excommunicating him because original jurisdiction belonged to his local Session. It did not adjudicate the charges’ merits or order a remand.
first_summary: A communicant member appealed Presbytery’s adjudication of charges against him and his excommunication. The SJC reversed because the Session of his local church, not Presbytery or its Special Judicial Commission, was the proper court of original jurisdiction for judicial action and censure against a communicant member.
summary: A communicant member appealed Presbytery’s findings of guilt and censure of excommunication. The SJC reversed Presbytery’s and its Special Judicial Commission’s actions because original jurisdiction over judicial proceedings against a local church’s communicant member belonged to that church’s Session. The decision was jurisdictional: it neither resolved the underlying charges nor directed a remand or acquittal.
